Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Concurrent Medication: Allowed: - Procrit. - Amphotericin B (1 mg/kg up to 5 days/week). - Prophylaxis treatment as per ACTG recommendations for Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia. - Acyclovir (up to 1000 mg/day PO; for > 1000 mg/day PO or for any IV dose, suggest interrupting ddC). - Ketoconazole (up to 10 mg/kg/day). - Nystatin. - Aspirin, acetaminophen, sedatives, and barbiturates (for up to 72 hours). - Isoniazid (INH), if there is no evidence of peripheral neuropathy at entry. Children should receive pyridoxine, 25 - 50 mg/day to avoid possible INH-associated neuropathy. - Trimethoprim / sulfamethoxazole (T/S). - Immunoglobulin therapy. - Aerosolized pentamidine. - Drugs with little nephro-, hepato-, cytotoxicity that the patient has been taking and tolerating well for an ongoing condition.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: Patient is on metformin for diabetes, which is not explicitly listed in allowed medications. The criteria allow 'drugs with little nephro-, hepato-, cytotoxicity' if tolerated, but metformin's inclusion is not definitively confirmed or denied by the data.

Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Concurrent Treatment: Allowed: - Immunoglobulin therapy. - Nutritional support (for children with wasting syndrome and/or malnutritional) including hyperalimentation (TPN) of dietary supplements.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: Patient is an adult with no indication of wasting syndrome or malnutrition.

Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: AMENDED: - Patients enrolled in ACTG 051 may participate in ACTG 138 if they show intolerance to AZT or show disease progression after 6 months of AZT therapy and meet entry criteria for the study.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: No mention of AZT use or intolerance in the patient's history.

Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Patients must have the following: - Absence of acute opportunistic infection at time of entry. - However, if patient is successfully treated for opportunistic infection and has remained stable for 2 weeks after treatment, the patient is then allowed to enter the study.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: No evidence of acute opportunistic infection or recent treatment for such infections.

Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Parent or guardian available to give written informed consent.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: Written informed consent has been obtained.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Co-existing Condition: AMENDED: - 04-25-91 Additional excluded symptoms and conditions: - Symptomatic cardiomyopathy.
Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: Patient has ischemic cardiomyopathy confirmed by heart biopsy.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Concurrent Medication: Excluded: - Other antiviral agents, biological modifiers, and investigational medications.
Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: Patient is on metformin, not excluded antiviral agents.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Patients with the following are excluded: - Acute bacterial infections requiring IV or oral antibiotic treatment at time of entry.
Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: No evidence of acute bacterial infections requiring antibiotics.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Prior Medication: Excluded: - Antiretroviral agents (other than zidovudine (AZT) or didanosine (ddI)) within 4 weeks of entry.
Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: No antiretroviral agents mentioned in the patient's history.

Recap: Patient has symptomatic cardiomyopathy (exclusion violation) but meets most inclusion criteria. Metformin use is unclear under allowed medications.
